prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Summary of key proposals (ideology-free)

Economy and investment
- Create a Sustainable Investment Board; launch a £400bn National Transformation Fund, including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund.
- Establish a National Investment Bank with Regional Development Banks and a Post Bank to expand lending, especially to SMEs and communities.
- Tighten financial regulation to shift capital from polluting assets to green investment; change London Stock Exchange listing rules to require climate responsibility.

Climate, energy and industry
- Target most emissions reductions by 2030; create 1m climate jobs.
- Deliver ~90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon sources by 2030; expand offshore/onshore wind, solar, tidal; retain new nuclear; ban fracking.
- Retrofit almost all homes to high efficiency; roll out heat pumps, district heat networks, storage and grid upgrades.
- Impose a windfall tax on oil firms; support a just transition for energy workers.
- Bring energy and water into public ownership; create a UK National Energy Agency and 14 Regional Energy Agencies.
- Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; support steel, hydrogen, CCS; build gigafactories; develop plastics remanufacturing; green public procurement.

Transport
- Bring rail and buses into public ownership; reinstate cut bus routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils control services.
- Nationwide rail electrification; HS2 to Scotland; “Crossrail for the North”; expand rail freight.
- Increase cycling/walking funding; aim to end new combustion car sales by 2030; invest in EV charging and zero‑emission public fleets.

Environment, food and animal welfare
- New Climate and Environment Emergency Bill; Clean Air Act; increased flood defence funding.
- Legally binding nature recovery targets; major tree planting; stronger protected areas; environmental tribunal.
- Producer responsibility for waste; deposit return schemes.
- Establish a Right to Food; halve food bank use in a year and end need in three years; net‑zero food production by 2040.
- Strengthen animal welfare, including ending certain wildlife culls and harmful trapping.

Public finances and services
- Fund services via fairer taxation (higher rates only on top earners; no VAT rise); major anti‑avoidance drive.
- Presumption to insource public services; phase out PFI; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for estates.
- Public sector pay: year‑one 5% rise and above‑inflation increases thereafter.

Health and social care
- Health spending to rise by 4.3% annually; end outsourcing; invest in capital, IT and diagnostics; free prescriptions and basic dentistry.
- Expand mental health access, modernise facilities, boost children’s services.
- Create a National Care Service; free personal care for older people; cap lifetime care costs; improve care worker pay and conditions; raise Carer’s Allowance.

Education and skills
- Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; extend paid maternity leave to 12 months.
- More school funding; class sizes capped at 30 in primaries; scrap SATs; arts premium; stronger SEND support.
- Bring academies/free schools under local oversight; free school meals for all primary pupils.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 3 and six years at Levels 4–6); abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; post‑qualification admissions.
- Climate Apprenticeships funded via reformed levy.

Work, rights and corporate governance
- Real Living Wage of at least £10/hour for all 16+; ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral bargaining; ban unpaid internships.
- Target 32‑hour average full‑time week within a decade with no loss of pay.
- Create a Workers’ Protection Agency; require one‑third worker‑elected directors; Inclusive Ownership Funds in large firms.

Policing, justice and security
- Recruit additional police and PCSOs; restore neighbourhood policing.
- Reunify probation; restore legal aid; presumption against short prison sentences; strengthen victims’ rights.
- Overhaul cybersecurity; review border controls.

Housing
- Build over 1m social homes in a decade; at least 150k/yr by end of term, including 100k council homes; end Right to Buy.
- Rent controls; end no‑fault evictions; national licensing and standards; zero‑carbon homes standard; £1bn fire safety fund; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Create a Sovereign Land Trust; “use it or lose it” powers on stalled sites.

Digital, culture, media, sport, gambling
- Free full‑fibre broadband nationwide by 2030 via a public provider; Charter of Digital Rights.
- Cultural Capital Fund; arts premium; media plurality reforms; protect free TV licences for over‑75s.
- Football governance reforms; curb gambling advertising; new Gambling Act with limits and levy.

Migration, refugees, social security, equalities
- End hostile policies; end indefinite detention; close specified detention centres; protect family reunion; declaratory rights for EU nationals; safe routes and right to work for refugees.
- Replace Universal Credit; interim fixes (end five‑week wait and sanctions; scrap benefit cap and two‑child limit; raise Local Housing Allowance).
- Strengthen disability rights and benefits; increase Carer’s Allowance.
- Maintain pension triple lock; keep state pension age at 66; fair remedy for affected women; transparent pensions dashboard.

Constitution and governance
- Abolish the House of Lords, replacing it with an elected Senate after a constitutional convention.
- Votes at 16; automatic voter registration; repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; stricter lobbying/donations rules; extend FOI.

Foreign policy and defence
- War Powers Act; increase diplomatic capacity; human‑rights‑led trade and arms export controls; climate diplomacy; recognise Palestine within a two‑state framework.
- Maintain NATO commitment and spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; renew the nuclear deterrent; support veterans; publish defence industrial and shipbuilding strategies.

Brexit
- Negotiate a customs‑union‑based deal with close single market alignment and put it to a confirmatory referendum alongside remain within six months; implement the result; guarantee citizens’ rights.

TEXT_C:
Summary (max 500 words)

Overall approach
- A 10-year Green New Deal to reach net-zero emissions by 2030 while expanding jobs, infrastructure, and public services. Investment: over £100bn a year (plus UBI), alongside major tax reform, targeted savings, and £94.4bn a year of public capital borrowing to upgrade infrastructure, catalysing an estimated £50bn a year of private investment.

Energy
- Rapid scale-up of renewables (around 70% of electricity from wind by 2030, with major solar, tidal, hydro, geothermal). End fossil fuel subsidies; rising Carbon Tax on extraction/imports and embedded emissions; ban fracking; no new nuclear. Double grid capacity, expand storage, strengthen European interconnectors, enable community energy.

Housing and buildings
- Insulate every home by 2030; deep retrofit 1m homes a year; 1m homes with domestic renewables annually; replace gas boilers with heat pumps and other low-carbon heat; district heat networks. Build at least 100,000 new social homes per year to Passivhaus standards. Tighten building regs, prioritise renovation, and lift rented homes to EPC A by 2030.

Transport
- Make public transport cheaper than driving; invest £2.5bn/year in walking/cycling; electrify key rail; reopen lines; shift freight to rail; bring rail into public ownership over 10 years. Local control of buses and new tram systems. End new runways and additional road capacity; cancel HS2. End sales of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030; national EV charging. Frequent Flyer Levy; restrict flight advertising; Carbon Tax includes domestic aviation.

Industry and circular economy
- Support UK clean manufacturing; grants to replace high-carbon equipment; clean tech standards; regional mutual banks for green SMEs; £2bn/year for skills. Ten-year warranties and right-to-repair; ban single-use plastics; full producer responsibility for packaging; near-100% recycling infrastructure; early CCS for steel/cement.

Food, farming, forestry, nature
- Ten-year transition to agroecology; refocus subsidies; cut pesticide use by at least 50% by 2022 and ban most harmful products; plant 700m trees; 50% of farms in agroforestry by 2030; rewilding via planning; urban food growing; flood prevention through nature-based solutions; prevent building on floodplains; moratorium on GM.

Income, work, housing security
- Phased Universal Basic Income: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disability/lone parents; retain Housing Benefit where needed; child supplements; partly funded by Carbon Tax. Living Wage £12 (including ages 16–21); fair work rules for gig economy; cap pay ratios at 10:1; 35 hours free childcare from 9 months; rent controls tied to local incomes; end no-fault evictions; community right to buy land.

Democracy and government
- Proportional representation for Parliament and local councils; votes at 16; elected second chamber; citizens’ assemblies and a People’s Constitution; stronger transparency and lobbying rules; media plurality measures; Digital Bill of Rights. New department for the Green New Deal with annual carbon budgets; Future Generations Act and minister. End arms export promotion.

Local government and services
- +£10bn/year to councils; £3bn/year climate adaptation; £4.5bn/year free home social care for over-65s (England); devolved transport and skills; expanded social housing; homelessness prevention; participatory budgeting. NHS: +£6bn/year (plus £1bn for nursing education), roll back privatisation, expand community and mental health, and reproductive health (including PrEP). Education: +£4bn/year; smaller classes; end high-stakes testing/Ofsted; restore arts; scrap tuition fees; write off recent student debt; expand adult education; climate/nature curriculum and a Nature GCSE.

Justice, drugs, discrimination, animals
- Shift from short prison sentences to restorative justice; women’s centres; invest in youth services and community policing. Replace prohibition with regulated, evidence-based drug policy; pardons for minor possession/supply; cannabis legalisation and regulated sales; heroin-assisted treatment; safe consumption rooms; alcohol minimum pricing. Cross-government strategy on inequality; humane immigration system; end detention centres; misogyny as hate crime; enhanced protections for LGBTIQA+ and disabled people; animal sentience in law; ban hunting and live exports; end badger cull; phase out animal testing.

Tax, land, spending
- Consolidated Income Tax treating income from wealth like work; abolish non-dom status; raise Corporation Tax to 24%; tougher anti-avoidance and HMRC independence. Replace Council Tax and Business Rates with a Land Value Tax phased over 10 years, with protections for low-income and pensioner homeowners. Cancel Trident replacement, major road building, airport expansions, HS2; end Help to Buy and the NHS internal market. Support small business via regional mutual banks, prompt payment, targeted VAT cuts in hospitality/culture, and a higher Employment Allowance.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile.
